probes.query: Find the useScrollToBottom hook in the TypeScript source (.ts) — the one that tracks whether the message list is scrolled to the bottom and exposes a scrollToBottom callback.
expectedFacts: useScrollToBottom is declared in hooks/use-scroll-to-bottom.tsx (a .tsx file, not a .ts file); it keeps containerRef/endRef plus an isAtBottom state and returns a scrollToBottom callback. No .ts (non-tsx) file declares it.
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: WRONG-EXTENSION pathology. Query says '.ts' but the hook lives in a .tsx. Verified: `rg -n 'export function useScrollToBottom' -g'*.ts' -g'*.tsx' .` -> ONLY hooks/use-scroll-to-bottom.tsx:3 `export function useScrollToBottom() {`. `rg -n useScrollToBottom -g'*.ts' . | grep -v '\.tsx'` -> NONE (the only other reference is an import in hooks/use-messages.tsx:4). Agent must relax the file-extension filter (.ts -> .tsx) before relaxing the search term.

probes.query: Where does gin actually marshal a protobuf message into the HTTP response body and set the application/x-protobuf content type? I want the response renderer, not the generated message code.
expectedFacts: The hand-authored render.ProtoBuf renderer in render/protobuf.go marshals the response via proto.Marshal(r.Data.(proto.Message)) and writes the application/x-protobuf content type (protobufContentType). The bulk of the 'proto' hits are in the autogenerated testdata/protoexample/test.pb.go, which is not the renderer.
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: FLOODING TRAP: the 'proto' literal floods the autogenerated testdata/protoexample/test.pb.go (header line 1 `// Code generated by protoc-gen-go. DO NOT EDIT.`, 81 'proto' hits across 298 lines — `grep -c proto testdata/protoexample/test.pb.go` -> 81), by far the densest match. The real source-of-truth is the small hand-authored renderer: `grep -n 'type ProtoBuf struct\|func (r ProtoBuf) Render\|proto.Marshal' render/protobuf.go` -> :14, :21, :24 (`bytes, err := proto.Marshal(r.Data.(proto.Message))`); protobufContentType = []string{"application/x-protobuf"} at render/protobuf.go:18. Agent must negative-space-route around the generated testdata file.

probes.query: How does ripgrep pick the default number of search threads when the user doesn't pass --threads, and which conditions force it to run single-threaded?
expectedFacts: Inside HiArgs::from_low_args the thread count is forced to 1 when --sort is set (low.sort.is_some()) or only one file is being searched (paths.is_one_file); otherwise it uses an explicit --threads value, and if none was given it defaults to std::thread::available_parallelism() capped at 12 (.min(12))
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: Behavioral (the heuristic, not a named fn). Verified: `grep -n 'pub(crate) fn from_low_args(mut low: LowArgs)' crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs` -> :113 (impl HiArgs @108). The thread-count logic is an inline `let threads = ...` binding at hiargs.rs:168-174: `if low.sort.is_some() || paths.is_one_file { 1 } else if let Some(threads) = low.threads { threads } else { std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get()).min(12) }` (the .min(12) cap is at hiargs.rs:173). hard_for_tools: the answer is a `let` binding inside a long constructor, not a discrete function named after 'threads' (the threads() getter at hiargs.rs:853 is just `self.threads`).

Impl `grep -n 'private bool NetworkSUBSCRIBE(RespCommand cmd)' libs/server/Resp/PubSubCommands.cs` -> :129 (a RespServerSession partial); it calls `subscribeBroker.Subscribe(key, this)` at PubSubCommands.cs:173. Broker `grep -n 'public unsafe bool Subscribe(ArgSlice key, ServerSessionBase session)' libs/server/PubSub/SubscribeBroker.cs` -> :187 (class SubscribeBroker @19). hard_for_tools: the subscribe handler lives in a different partial file from the dispatch switch, and the actual bookkeeping is one more hop into the broker.

probes.query: When you construct a TypeToken<T> from a raw java.lang.reflect.Type, where does Gson normalize that type into a canonical form and resolve its raw Class? Find the TypeToken entry point and the internal type utility it delegates to.
expectedFacts: TypeToken's Type-taking constructor calls GsonTypes.canonicalize(type) to normalize the type and GsonTypes.getRawType(type) to derive the raw Class; both canonicalize and getRawType are implemented in internal/GsonTypes.java
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: Multi-file (public reflect helper -> internal type util). Verified: `grep -n 'public class TypeToken<T>' gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/reflect/TypeToken.java` -> :54; the private TypeToken(Type) ctor calls `GsonTypes.canonicalize(Objects.requireNonNull(type))` at TypeToken.java:82 and `GsonTypes.getRawType(this.type)` at TypeToken.java:83. Impl `grep -n 'public final class GsonTypes\|public static Type canonicalize\|public static Class<?> getRawType' gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/GsonTypes.java` -> class@43, canonicalize@104, getRawType@128. hard_for_tools: the entry point is in the public reflect package but the actual logic lives in the internal GsonTypes utility, two packages away.

probes.query: Where are Fastify's FST_ERR_* error codes actually defined? I'm looking for the TypeScript error-codes definition (the FastifyErrorCodes typing), e.g. the FST_ERR_NOT_FOUND code object.
expectedFacts: The FST_ERR_* codes are created at runtime in lib/errors.js: a `codes` object whose entries (e.g. FST_ERR_NOT_FOUND) are built with createError from @fastify/error. types/errors.d.ts only declares the FastifyErrorCodes TYPE (a Record over the code names) and contains no runtime definitions.
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: WRONG-EXTENSION pathology. Query points at the TypeScript declaration (.d.ts/.ts), but the real definitions are JavaScript. The decoy `grep -n FastifyErrorCodes types/errors.d.ts` -> :3 `export type FastifyErrorCodes = Record<` is only a type union of code NAMES (no values, no createError). The real source: `grep -n '^const codes = {\|FST_ERR_NOT_FOUND: createError' lib/errors.js` -> :5 (`const codes = {`), :9 (`FST_ERR_NOT_FOUND: createError(`); `grep -c FST_ERR_ lib/errors.js` -> 182 codes; createError imported from @fastify/error at lib/errors.js:3. Agent must relax the .ts/.d.ts extension expectation and route to lib/errors.js.

expectedFacts: AppContext.pop (ctx.py) calls self.app.do_teardown_request(self, exc) when a request is present, then self.app.do_teardown_appcontext(self, exc); do_teardown_request (app.py) runs the teardown_request_funcs and sends request_tearing_down, while do_teardown_appcontext runs teardown_appcontext_funcs and sends appcontext_tearing_down
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: Multi-file (context object -> app methods). Verified: `grep -n '    def pop(self, exc: BaseException' src/flask/ctx.py` -> :446; the pop body calls `self.app.do_teardown_request(self, exc)` at ctx.py:490 and `self.app.do_teardown_appcontext(self, exc)` at ctx.py:496. probes.query: Where is highway's public Now() timer entry point declared versus implemented, and how is a raw tick count converted into elapsed seconds?
expectedFacts: hwy::Now() is declared HWY_DLLEXPORT in hwy/timer.h and defined in hwy/timer.cc, where it multiplies the raw tick count (timer::Start()) by 1.0/InvariantTicksPerSecond() to return seconds; the inline SecondsSince(Timestamp) helper in timer.h subtracts a stored timestamp to give elapsed seconds
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: Multi-file header/impl split. Verified: declaration `grep -n 'HWY_DLLEXPORT double Now();' hwy/timer.h` -> :61; definition `grep -n 'HWY_DLLEXPORT double Now() {' hwy/timer.cc` -> :122 (body: `static const double mul = 1.0 / InvariantTicksPerSecond(); return static_cast<double>(timer::Start()) * mul;`). `grep -n 'static inline double SecondsSince' hwy/timer.h` -> :91. Timestamp ctor (timer.h:87) seeds t = platform::Now().

probes.query: If a Flow emits values faster than the debounce timeout, which emissions actually get through, and what does debounce do if the timeout is zero?
expectedFacts: Flow.debounce(timeoutMillis) filters out any value that is followed by a newer value within timeoutMillis (so back-to-back fast emissions are dropped and only the latest after a quiet gap is emitted); it require()s a non-negative timeout and, when timeoutMillis == 0L, returns the original flow unchanged (no debouncing)
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: Behavioral (emission semantics + zero-timeout edge case). Verified: `grep -n 'public fun <T> Flow<T>.debounce(timeoutMillis: Long)' kotlinx-coroutines-core/common/src/flow/operators/Delay.kt` -> :61; body `require(timeoutMillis >= 0L) { "Debounce timeout should not be negative" }` at Delay.kt:62, `if (timeoutMillis == 0L) return this` at Delay.kt:63, then debounceInternal { timeoutMillis }. KDoc example (Delay.kt ~40-60) shows fast emissions 1,2 dropped -> output 3,4,5; 'does not emit anything as long as the original flow emits items faster than every timeoutMillis'. Duration/selector overloads also exist in the same file.

probes.query: Which Sinatra helper streams a file from disk back to the client as the response (handling content-type, attachment disposition and a missing-file 404)?
expectedFacts: Helpers#send_file(path, opts) sets the content type (from opts[:type] or the file extension), optionally sets an attachment disposition/filename, serves the file via Rack::Files#serving, and rescues Errno::ENOENT to call not_found (404)
probes.author: rotation-author
probes.notes: Literal-lookup. Verified: `grep -n '    def send_file(path, opts' lib/sinatra/base.rb` -> :426. Body (base.rb:426-447) sets content_type from opts[:type] or File.extname(path), applies attachment(filename, disposition), serves via Rack::Files.new(...).serving(request, path), halts with the status + body, and `rescue Errno::ENOENT` -> not_found.
